tiles.name: Slab
tiles.explanation:
A floor of stone slabs. Unlike grass or dirt, a slab floor is meant to show its tiles: each slab has a dark rim round its edge, so the floor reads as a grid of separate stones. Here the seam is part of the design, and it still has to match: the rim on the right fits against the rim on the left of the next copy.

The rim is lit like a raised edge, with paler flecks down the sides and the darkest color along the bottom.

![Slabs, repeated](examples/plain-repeated.png)

tiles.name: Worn slab
tiles.explanation: The worn slab is the same stone with a few pits: single darker pixels with paler ones beside them. Small marks like these make the floor look used without changing its shape.

tiles.name: Cracked slab
tiles.explanation:
The cracked slab has thin cracks in it. A crack is a dark line with a pale pixel beside it: dark for the gap, pale for the broken edge catching the light, the same trick as the rim. Mix the three slabs and the floor looks old and walked on.

![The three slabs mixed](examples/mixed.png)
